newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Probe launched in SAfrica Reunert trading.
newsitem.headline: Probe launched in SAfrica Reunert trading.

text.p: A probe has been launched into trading in South African electronics group Reunert Ltd, a Securities Regulation Panel (SRP) source said on Monday.
The firm issued a profit warning around Wednesday lunchtime, but the group's stock had earlier attracted heavy trade that had seen it touch a year low of 12.50 rand in the morning.
"It is possible that some of the news might have leaked out...we are looking at it," the SRP source said.
The firm said it would not match the first half earnings of the previous year and a reduction of about 15 percent in profits could be expected.
At 0900 GMT on Monday the firm's stock had lost further ground to set another new year low of 12.35 rand.
A company spokesman told Reuters that the SRP had been in touch with the firm about a possible leak of information to the market.

However, the spokesman said that the company's impression was that no untoward trading had occurred. "From what they (the SRP) have seen from trading and the type of trading there was, there doesn't seem to have been any leak," he said.

The SRP source confirmed that the heavy volume of shares in the group appeared to be a natural reflection of a heavy day's trade on the bourse, but added that the movement of the share price did warrant checking.
South Africa has an unwanted reputation as a haven of insider trading, although new legislation to tackle unfair dealings in stocks and bonds could be in place by year-end.
A government-appointed task group on insider trading set up last year is set to deliver its proposals on how to tackle the problem.

Earlier this year the apparent leaking of news of a big shake-up at car firm Automakers Ltd caused a stir. The firm's share shot up ahead of news that majority shareholder Sankorp would make a payout to minorities at a substantial premium to the prevailing market price.
